subject.title: Fix OpenClaw command tool runtime path

question: Should the Nix Codex launcher replace inherited HOME for existing installations, and if so what supported migration and ownership rules protect existing Codex credentials, settings, and native-home profile state?
rationale: The fix’s mechanism intentionally changes an upstream compatibility contract and can either hide state or stop startup. Source inspection cannot establish whether maintainers accept that migration cost or prefer an upstream/path-only design.

options.title: Preserve existing HOME state
options.body: Redesign the integration so runtime tools are exposed without replacing an existing Codex HOME, or add a tested migration that explicitly preserves the supported state.

options.title: Accept managed HOME as a migration
options.body: Keep the isolated HOME design only with documented upgrade behavior, safe treatment of existing profile paths, and fresh-install plus upgrade proof.

options.title: Pause for upstream support
options.body: Hold the launcher change until OpenClaw exposes a supported per-agent command PATH contract independent of HOME.

recommendation.title: Preserve existing HOME state
recommendation.body: Redesign the integration so runtime tools are exposed without replacing an existing Codex HOME, or add a tested migration that explicitly preserves the supported state.

likelyOwner.reason: This maintainer authored the current implementation and is the named repository-policy maintainer most directly connected to the design choice.
